Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b08/review-experiment-m1ad5us3/call-18e896beb4d0404da2afa4470e38c1a3/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'command -v pdftotext; command -v pdftoppm; command -v pdfinfo; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pymupdf','PIL']:
    spec=importlib.util.find_spec(name)
    print(name, spec.origin if spec else None)
from pathlib import Path
print('pdf bytes',Path('manuscript.pdf').stat().st_size)
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:', len(reader.pages))
print('Metadata:', reader.metadata)
out=Path('tmp/pdfs');out.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
text=''
for i,p in enumerate(reader.pages,1):
    t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    (out/f'page-{i:02}.txt').write_text(t)
    text += f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+t
(out/'manuscript.txt').write_text(text)
print(text[:38000])
PY"

strengths: Soundness: For sufficiently smooth risks with Haar augmentation, Lemma 4 and Proposition 1 correctly establish the risk-averaging and gradient identities. These support preservation of the layerwise equivariant subspace and equality of stationary points within it.
Significance: Distinguishing preservation of equivariance from stability against transverse perturbations addresses a useful question about augmentation versus architectural constraints.

Originality: Applying the induced group action to nonlinear MLP parameters provides a useful optimization-focused synthesis. The originality is moderate, with the main machinery following standard group-averaging arguments.

Presentation and reproducibility: The assumptions, numbered results, and supporting proofs make the argument accessible. The manuscript supplies architectural and projection details, 30 repetitions per experiment, a code URL, and computational-resource information.

Limitations and ethics: The local, idealized scope and unexplained rotation results are explicitly acknowledged. These disclosures are appropriate, and no material ethical concerns are apparent in the synthetic-data and MNIST experiments.
weaknesses: The experiments do not establish the claimed instability. Section 5.1 interprets increasing distance from the equivariant subspace as evidence of instability, but finite sampled augmentation introduces transverse gradient noise even when the exact augmented flow is stable. Figure 1 provides no transverse Hessian measurements, controlled perturbation tests, or exact-augmentation controls to distinguish these explanations. Averaging all four rotations would provide a direct control for Experiment 3.

Proposition 3 requires correction. Since R_eqv(A)=R(P_E A), this objective is constant along E_perp and cannot have strict local minima in the full parameter space when E_perp is nontrivial. Part (ii) must refer to minima restricted to E. Moreover, the proofs assume positive-definite Hessians, which strict local minima need not possess. Section 4.2's assertion that the Hessian spectrum completely determines stability also needs qualification for zero eigenvalues and evolving trajectories.

Equation (3) is false under the stated assumptions: averaging predictions before applying a loss generally differs from averaging losses. For an invariant scalar-output task, predictions +1 and -1 across two transformations with target zero yield squared augmentation loss 1 but feature-averaged loss 0. Convexity provides a Jensen inequality, not the asserted equality. Although the main gradient identity does not depend on this error, the comparison with feature averaging needs revision.

The practical interpretation exceeds the proven scope. Corollary 2 concerns parameters within the chosen layerwise equivariant subspace E. Networks outside E can still implement equivariant functions through interactions between layers. Consequently, Section 6's claim that manifest equivariance excludes no equivariant configurations is not established. Equality of stationary-point sets also does not independently establish convergence or which minima training reaches.

Reproducibility and correspondence with the theory remain incomplete. The manuscript does not specify N_aug or batch size, although both directly affect the sampling noise relevant to Figure 1. Numerical precision is especially relevant to the reported transverse shifts near 10^-7. Batch normalization also changes the fixed, samplewise network model used in the analysis; the inference-time equivariance assertion does not justify the claimed training-flow correspondence without specifying and analyzing the training-time normalization and its parameters.
